_readme: Content for the dashboard's Analyst Views tab. Each 'view' is a short paraphrase of a public statement, with a link to where it was said and the date. Every entry must be checked against its source by a human before publishing. 'check' names a live comparison in dashboard_site/index.html (ANALYST_CHECKS); null means the view isn't something this system's data can test. Refresh roughly quarterly; the page flags any analyst whose views_as_of is more than 90 days old.

analysts.name: Ray Dalio
analysts.lens: Long-term debt cycles: when government debt outgrows the ability to service it, the endgame is higher rates or money printing, and hard assets like gold outperform.

themes.view: Says the government's finances are "at an inflection point" and a debt crisis could come in about three years, "give or take two," if the course isn't changed.
themes.if_differs: The fiscal-pressure checks (interest burden, primary deficit, spending share) would need to start pointing to stress.

themes.view: Recommends underweighting bonds. Argues weakening demand for US debt could force rates higher, or force the Fed to print money to buy it.
themes.if_differs: The 10-year yield would need to rise into this system's elevated zone (above 4.3%).

themes.theme: Gold as a hedge against money printing
themes.view: Suggests holding 10–15% in gold (and "a bit" of bitcoin), because non-government money should do well if currencies are devalued.
themes.if_differs: Gold would need to stop trading like a normal interest-rate asset — its usual inverse link to real yields breaking down is the debasement-hedge signature this system looks for.

themes.view: Warns "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down."
themes.if_differs: This system's Taylor Rule check would need to show the Fed funds rate below what inflation and unemployment alone justify.

themes.view: Urges fixing the deficit now, while the economy is still healthy, since a recession would require more government spending (CNBC's summary).
themes.if_differs: The Sahm Rule recession indicator would need to be back in its normal range.

themes.view: His crisis window is one to five years out, depending on events like military conflict or political change.
themes.note: This system looks weeks to months ahead. It can't confirm or rule out a multi-year call; it would only register one once the stress reaches markets.

analysts.name: Ritesh Jain
analysts.lens: Global liquidity and capital flows: financial repression keeps rates below inflation, the dollar weakens, and real assets beat financial ones.

themes.view: "Long yields are revolting earlier than I expected." Calls long-duration Western government bonds "certificates of confiscation" under financial repression.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: The 10-year yield would need to rise into this system's elevated zone (above 4.3%).

themes.view: Says financial repression plus re-industrialization "naturally weakens the dollar"; in March, said the trade-weighted dollar had broken its multi-year uptrend.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Nothing Stops This Train

themes.if_differs: The broad trade-weighted dollar would need to be below both its level a year ago and its 200-day average.

themes.view: Structurally bullish — central banks now hold more gold than Treasuries — but trades it on China's liquidity impulse: cut to about 3% in February, rebuilt as that impulse resumed.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: Gold would need to stop trading like a normal interest-rate asset — its usual inverse link to real yields breaking down is the monetary-shift signature this system looks for.

themes.view: Expects US inflation to settle at 3–4% rather than below 2% — "a view rather than something anyone can verify today."

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: Headline CPI inflation would need to hold at 3% or more year over year.

themes.view: Said in November 2025 a correction "could be ten per cent or more" (reprinted in August 2026). Calls today's market a "rolling bubble" that deflates rather than bursts.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: This system would need confirmed crash indicators turning RED, or its hazard model moving to High.

themes.view: "I expect the economy to weaken from the fourth quarter" of 2026, as tax and tariff support fades.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: The Sahm Rule recession indicator would need to rise out of its normal range (0.3 or higher).

themes.view: Flags record US margin debt — $1.53 trillion in June, up more than 50% year over year.

source.title: Pinetree Macro — Two Years of Return in Two Months

themes.if_differs: Margin-debt growth would need to rank in the top quarter of its own history.
